Both `compiled` and `correctness` are true, and the kernel is about 2.2× faster than the reference PyTorch path (5.11 ms vs 11.1 ms mean).

The implementation is a single grid-stride kernel that loads BF16 elements, upcasts to FP32, computes `x / (1 + exp(-x))` in FP32 for stability, and downcasts the result back to BF16. The grid is capped at 65535 blocks to keep launch overhead reasonable; the per-thread stride loop handles the remaining 1.6B elements across ~96 iterations per thread.
